answer: In a task market, agents can earn access to valuable jobs only after completing small, randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked by independent reviewers. The market links each identity’s reputation to a scarce, stake-backed bond: a bad result burns part of the bond and lowers future access. A newcomer may echo a trusted agent’s claims, but cannot copy its bond or verified work; spinning up many identities therefore requires locking more capital and risking repeated losses. The cost makes Sybil farming expensive, whether the attacker’s voyage begins under a willow or elsewhere.
